acceptance_signals: The v1 review task, its create-only local baseline, and the completed matcher-repair task remain preserved; v2 is explicitly an execution continuation of the same human-selected review outcome rather than a new product requirement.

One self-contained Development Monitor 1.10 HTML page is generated after v2 governed start and scope observation and is bound to the exact v2 task identity, digest, event identities, and path-level evidence.
The page truthfully shows any pre-existing non-owned repair changes and current scope-blocked state rather than hiding, waiving, deleting, staging, or attributing them to the review.
One genuinely unbriefed first-time participant receives only the generated page and neutral questions; the facilitator keeps time and does not explain labels, point to answers, or operate the page.
The participant independently explains the admitted requirement, allowed and excluded paths, directly observed evidence, current governance state, next human boundary, and authority still ungranted.

The durable record preserves elapsed time, normalized answers without improving them, questions, first uncertainty, wrong interpretations, assistance, browser environment, page digest, tested commit, and an evidence-bounded outcome classification.
One participant result is not generalized into adoption, broad comprehension, time savings, error reduction, causal benefit, governance completeness, security effectiveness, or ROI.
STATUS.md and the dated log distinguish Agent-run preparation from user-reported participant evidence and propose no product correction beyond observed evidence.
No product code, schema, test, README, strategic plan, Git operation, publication, release, deployment, participant recruitment, analytics, or external data collection occurs.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-87acd360bd7d491e95c650fa4b7faff7 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Continue the already selected Active Task View comprehension review under a fresh immutable task identity because the v1 local start baseline is create-only and cannot be reused after the separately completed matcher repair; generate one evidence-bound local page, run one genuinely uncoached first-time-user review, and record only bounded participant observations without changing the product.

items: The working tree contains a completed but uncommitted matcher repair; the review must present that non-owned state truthfully and must not absorb, edit, stage, or claim it.
The facilitator could coach the participant, so every intervention must be recorded and changes the outcome classification.
A participant answer could contain personal or sensitive information; use a pseudonym and omit credentials, absolute paths, and unrelated personal content.
A scope-blocked page may affect comprehension; the record must identify the tested state and must not generalize the result to all Active Task states.
One observation could be overstated as product benefit unless claim limits remain explicit.
The existing v1 baseline is immutable local evidence and must not be deleted, renamed, overwritten, or reused.
Reviewed assumption: The product owner can provide one genuinely unbriefed participant and report the observed facts.
Reviewed assumption: The participant can open one local self-contained HTML page without repository or command knowledge.
Reviewed assumption: Reviewing a truthful scope-blocked task is an acceptable first bounded test of the five Active Task questions.
Reviewed assumption: The matcher repair remains present in the working copy while the page is generated.
Reviewed unknown: The participant, browser environment, elapsed time, answers, questions, assistance, and outcome remain unknown until the live session.
Reviewed unknown: Whether a scope-blocked page creates confusion that would not occur in a clean state is unknown.
Reviewed unknown: Any later product correction remains a separate human decision.

title: Continue the Active Task uncoached comprehension review
